rq: joint identification of raw-language equivalence and latent intervention-target partition
result: NeurIPS 2024 unaligned Shared Component Analysis establishes that lack of paired cross-modal samples alone does not preclude identification of a shared latent block under explicit linear mixture and distributional/structural assumptions. However, matching unpaired modality distributions does not identify the class-level language-to-target coupling, semantic partitions, or merge/split ontology: different denotation maps can preserve both modality marginals, shared-component distributions, and all distribution-matching objectives. Official code was audited at commit d62d2940f6d4ac471fe871614730d69f1b4f4ea5. A positive RQ now requires an observable cross-system dependence law rather than only matched marginals or an assumed common source.
